title: BLF Controlled Human Review Pilot (40 Items)

items.context: Directing an esteemed guest or citizen in public notice or formal discourse.
items.intended_meaning: Please remain calm.
items.phenomenon: হওয়া Honorific Imperative vs Present Indicative
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('হোন') is the standard 2nd person honorific imperative.
items.uncertainty_basis: Orthographic confusion in digital texts between indicative 'হন' and imperative 'হোন'.

items.context: Stating that you did not give something to someone.
items.intended_meaning: I did not give the book.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('দিইনি') is canonical standard, B ('দেইনি') is accepted colloquial.
items.uncertainty_basis: Vowel height harmony variation in 1st person standard Cholit.

items.context: Stating that you did not take money.
items.intended_meaning: I did not take money.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('নিইনি') is canonical standard, B ('নেইনি') is colloquial.
items.uncertainty_basis: Register calibration between literary standard and spoken colloquial.

items.context: Talking to a friend (ordinary 2nd person) about learning a skill.
items.intended_meaning: Haven't you learned the work yet?
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A and B are both accepted variants in standard BDSB.
items.uncertainty_basis: Orthographic vowel harmony in modern Bangla Academy spelling.

items.context: Narrating past event inception in news/story.
items.intended_meaning: The meeting started on time.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('হলো') is standard Cholit, B ('হল') is traditional Cholit.
items.uncertainty_basis: BA 2016 spelling reforms regarding final -o vowel marking.

items.context: 1st person future intention.
items.intended_meaning: I will become a teacher.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('হব') is normative Promito Bangla, B ('হবো') is common variant.
items.uncertainty_basis: Strict Bangla Academy orthography vs popular written practice.

items.context: Contrasting two objects pointed out by the speaker.
items.intended_meaning: Give this one, not that one.
items.system_hypothesis: Both A and B are natural; A highlights contrastive focus through overt -ke.
items.uncertainty_basis: Normative grammar rule claims -ke is animate-only, but corpus attests -ke on demonstratives.

items.context: Topicalizing a specific important letter.
items.intended_meaning: As for the letter, I have preserved it carefully.
items.system_hypothesis: Both A and B are attested; overt -ke in A marks discourse prominence.
items.uncertainty_basis: Register constraints on inanimate overt accusative marking.

items.context: Neutral transitive sentence putting a book on the table.
items.intended_meaning: He put the book on the table.
items.phenomenon: Definite Inanimate Object in Neutral Clause
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A (bare classifier 'বইটা') is the canonical neutral form.
items.uncertainty_basis: Whether 'বইটাকে' sounds overly marked in a non-contrastive neutral context.

items.context: Searching for medical assistance in emergency.
items.intended_meaning: We are searching for a doctor.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A (bare 'ডাক্তার') is natural for non-specific search.
items.uncertainty_basis: Interplay between humanness and non-specific referentiality.

items.context: Teacher summoning a specific newly admitted student.
items.intended_meaning: The teacher called the new student.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A (overt -ke) is strictly obligatory.
items.uncertainty_basis: Zero-case marking on specific human is generally considered ungrammatical.

items.context: Feeding a specific household cow.
items.intended_meaning: Feed grass to the cow.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A (overt -ke) is standard for specific individuated animals.
items.uncertainty_basis: Variation between bare classifier and overt -ke in rural vs urban standard.

items.context: Abstract issue under policy discussion.
items.intended_meaning: We must understand the issue deeply.
items.system_hypothesis: Both A and B are widely used in formal editorial BDSB.
items.uncertainty_basis: Acceptability of -ke on abstract non-physical nouns in standard prose.

items.context: Eating daily lunch.
items.intended_meaning: I eat rice every day.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A (bare 'ভাত') is obligatory; Candidate B is ungrammatical.
items.uncertainty_basis: Clear negative constraint on mass food terms taking -ke.

items.context: Describing multiple books on a shelf.
items.intended_meaning: Bring all those books.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A is standard; B and C with stacked suffixes are strictly invalid in BDSB.
items.uncertainty_basis: Morphotactic restriction barring singular classifier + plural marker.

items.context: Calling a group of specific children.
items.intended_meaning: Call the boys.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('ছেলেদেরকে') is standard formal; B is morphotactically illicit.
items.uncertainty_basis: Mutual exclusivity of -ta and -der.

items.context: Counting three pencils.
items.intended_meaning: Give me three pencils.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A is neutral; Candidate B carries definite/specific nuance.
items.uncertainty_basis: Pragmatic distinction between numeral+CLF+N vs N+numeral+CLF.

items.context: Referring to three persons respectfully.
items.intended_meaning: Three respected persons came.
items.phenomenon: Human vs Non-Human Classifier Selection (-jon vs -ti)
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('তিনজন') is obligatory for human honorific referents.
items.uncertainty_basis: Social constraint on using -ti/-ta for respected persons.

items.context: Diminutive or affectionate reference to a baby.
items.intended_meaning: The little child is laughing.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('-টি') is standard; B is regional/colloquial.
items.uncertainty_basis: Stylistic nuances of -টি (polite/small) vs -টা (neutral).

items.context: Indefinite plural quantification.
items.intended_meaning: Some people said this.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidates A and B are both standard BDSB.
items.uncertainty_basis: Preference of classifier attachment with count nouns.

items.context: Sudden cognitive realization after hearing news.
items.intended_meaning: He found out all the secrets.
items.candidate_a: সে খবরটা শুনেই সব জেনে ফেলল।
items.candidate_b: সে খবরটা শুনেই সব জেনে গেল।
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('জেনে ফেলল') is highly natural for irreversible cognitive achievement.
items.uncertainty_basis: Traditional telic restriction vs cognitive achievement compatibility.

items.context: Comprehending a complicated trick suddenly.
items.intended_meaning: I figured out his trick.
items.system_hypothesis: Both A ('বুঝে ফেললাম') and B ('বুঝে গেলাম') are natural; A highlights suddenness.
items.uncertainty_basis: Semantic nuances between telic 'phela' and transition 'jawa'.

items.context: Stative duration of staying somewhere.
items.intended_meaning: He remained in Dhaka.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('থেকে গেল') is grammatical; B ('থেকে ফেলল') is ungrammatical.
items.uncertainty_basis: Barring of pure stative verbs from combining with vector 'phela'.

items.context: Self-benefactive purchase.
items.intended_meaning: He bought the book for himself.
items.candidate_a: সে বাজার থেকে বইটা কিনে নিল।
items.candidate_b: সে বাজার থেকে বইটা কিনে দিল।
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A explicitly encodes self-directed benefit.
items.uncertainty_basis: Clear directional valency transfer of vector neoa/dewa.

items.context: Doing a favor for another person.
items.intended_meaning: The teacher wrote the letter for the student.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('লিখে দিলেন') is natural and polite for other-benefactive.
items.uncertainty_basis: Social and syntactic requirements for ditransitive vector dewa.

items.context: Rash, blurted-out utterance without thinking.
items.intended_meaning: He rashly blurted out the words.
items.candidate_a: সে না বুঝেই কথাটা বলে বসল।
items.candidate_b: সে না বুঝেই কথাটা বলে ফেলল।
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('বলে বসল') specifically encodes rash/improper action.
items.uncertainty_basis: Nuance distinction between 'বলে বসল' (inappropriate/rash) and 'বলে ফেলল' (accidental).

items.context: Sudden emotional eruption.
items.intended_meaning: The child suddenly burst out crying.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('কেঁদে উঠল') is the standard inceptive/eruptive expression.
items.uncertainty_basis: Strict selection of 'utha' with sound and emotion verbs.

items.context: Asking a neutral polar yes/no question about reading a book.
items.intended_meaning: Will you read the book?
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A (topic-adjacent) is canonical neutral; B puts focus on verb; C is formal tag-like.
items.uncertainty_basis: Determining canonical default placement in BDSB sentence synthesis.

items.context: Asking about destination vs asking for confirmation.
items.intended_meaning: Will you go to Dhaka tomorrow?
items.phenomenon: Polar Interrogative Placement with Time Adverbial
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A is standard; Candidate B focuses specifically on 'ঢাকা'.
items.uncertainty_basis: Scope interaction between polar particle 'কি' and adverbials.

items.context: Inquiring about what someone wants (Wh-question).
items.intended_meaning: What do you want?
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('কী') is orthographically standard for substantive 'what'.
items.uncertainty_basis: Widespread digital nonstandard habit of spelling 'কী' as 'কি'.

items.context: Inquiring about what someone ate.
items.intended_meaning: What did you eat in the morning?
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A is standard; Candidate B can be misread as polar ('Did you eat in the morning?').
items.uncertainty_basis: Syntactic ambiguity between Wh-question and Polar-question when spelled with 'কি'.

items.context: Negating a present perfect event (eating lunch).
items.intended_meaning: I haven't eaten lunch yet.
items.candidate_b: আমি এখনও দুপুরের খাবার খেয়েছি না।
items.candidate_c: আমি এখনও দুপুরের খাবার খাই নাই।
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A is standard; Candidate B ('*খেয়েছি না') is strictly ungrammatical.
items.uncertainty_basis: Strict morphological rule: perfective aspect negates with past stem + -ni.

items.context: Negating a simple present habitual action.
items.intended_meaning: I do not eat tea / I do not drink tea.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A (post-verbal 'না') is standard; Candidate C (pre-verbal) is restricted to subordinate clauses.
items.uncertainty_basis: Pre-verbal vs post-verbal negation position constraints in finite main clauses.

items.context: Subordinate conditional clause negation.
items.intended_meaning: If you don't go, I won't go either.
items.candidate_a: তুমি যদি না যাও, আমিও যাব না।
items.candidate_b: তুমি যদি যাও না, আমিও যাব না।
items.candidate_c: তুমি যদি যাবা না, আমিও যাইব না।
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A (pre-verbal 'না' in conditional) is standard and obligatory.
items.uncertainty_basis: Position flip of negation particle inside non-finite / conditional clauses.

items.context: Exclusive self-identification.
items.intended_meaning: I alone will go to the market.
items.phenomenon: Restrictive Focus Clitic '-ই' Scope (NP vs Predicate)
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A scopes over subject NP ('I alone'); B scopes over predicate ('certainly go').
items.uncertainty_basis: Scope differences depending on host attachment site of clitic -i.

items.context: Expressing shared common knowledge / prior consensus.
items.intended_meaning: As you know, I had already said this earlier.
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('তো' post-subject) marks contrastive topic / presupposition.
items.uncertainty_basis: Position flexibility and pragmatic nuances of 'তো'.

items.context: Asking a conversational tag question seeking agreement.
items.intended_meaning: You are coming tomorrow, right?
items.system_hypothesis: Both A and C are natural conversational tags; A seeks confirmation, C expresses expectation.
items.uncertainty_basis: Subtle pragmatic difference between sentence-final 'না' and 'তো'.

items.context: Concessive minimization.
items.intended_meaning: There is not even a single person present.
items.phenomenon: Scalar Concessive Clitic '-ও' on Minimal Quantifiers
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A ('একজন...ও') is standard scalar minimization ('not even one').
items.uncertainty_basis: Contrast between additive -o and restrictive -i on numerals.

items.context: Speaking to an elderly professor / dignitary.
items.intended_meaning: Where do you live?
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A is obligatory; Candidate C is ungrammatical due to honorific clash.
items.uncertainty_basis: Strict agreement invariant between subject honorificity and verb inflection.

items.context: Expressing mild surprise / evidential reminder.
items.intended_meaning: Look, he has actually arrived!
items.system_hypothesis: Candidate A and B express astonished evidential confirmation using 'যে'.
items.uncertainty_basis: Pragmatic distinction between complementizer 'যে' and emotive discourse marker 'যে'.
